en.p: There is a hyperbola $x^{2}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{35}=1$ with foci $\mathrm{F}(c,\,0)$ and $\mathrm{F'}(-c,\,0)\ (c>0)$. For a point $\mathrm{P}$ on this hyperbola in the first quadrant, take point $\mathrm{Q}$ on line $\mathrm{PF'}$ with $\overline{\mathrm{PQ}}=\overline{\mathrm{PF}}$. When triangles $\mathrm{QF'F}$ and $\mathrm{FF'P}$ are similar, the area of triangle $\mathrm{PFQ}$ is $\dfrac{q}{p}\sqrt{5}$. Find the value of $p+q$. (Given that $\overline{\mathrm{PF'}}<\overline{\mathrm{QF'}}$, and $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime natural numbers.) [4 points]
